svg.title: Pressure and oxygen partial pressure fall with height
svg.desc: Total pressure and oxygen partial pressure against altitude. Total pressure 1013 hPa at sea level, about 700 at 10,000 feet, about 500 (half) at 18,000 feet, about 375 at 25,000 and 250 at 34,000 feet. Oxygen stays about 21 percent of the air, so its partial pressure is 0.21 times the total: about 213 hPa at sea level, 147 at 10,000 feet and 105 at 18,000 feet.
svg.text: It is the partial pressure, not the percentage, that drives oxygen into the blood.
Nitrogen 78%, oxygen 21%, argon, CO2 and others 1%, at every height we fly.
